description: CRYPTO_SPEC §4.1: the value-write signature (Ed25519). value_signed_bytes = LP("<suite>/value-sig", project_id, environment_id, epoch, variable_id, version, nonce_hex, ciphertext_hex, prev_value_sig_hash_hex, writer_user_id, chain_head_hash_hex, chain_head_seq). The chain, keys, and DEKs reference chain-entries.json's canonical 12-entry chain
binary_encoding: nonce / ciphertext / hashes go into LP as lowercase hex strings (the same convention as chain-entries.json's binary_encoding). Numbers (epoch / version / chain_head_seq) are decimal-stringified
chain_reference: chain-entries.json: project_id = the genesis entry hash, chain_head_hash_hex = entries[chain_head_seq - 1].entry_hash_hex, writer keys = keys, DEKs = environment_deks (ciphertexts are real AES-GCM ciphertexts with the §4 LP as AAD). The canonical chain is 24 entries (2026-09-14 ES + PF1 — the meaning of the positives is unchanged; the negatives gained writer-environment-out-of-scope-at-head)

ghost.note: for writer-unknown-in-history (a key that exists nowhere in the chain history)

tenure_extension.note: the derived chain for key-from-other-tenure: after the canonical chain (24 entries), seq 25 re-adds user-member-0002 with new keys (remove → re-add = a different tenure). chain-entries.json itself is unchanged

vectors.name: v1-basic
vectors.note: version 1 (empty prev). The writer is the admin at head 12 (member or above); env-prod-0001's current epoch is 2

vectors.name: v2-chained
vectors.note: version 2. prev = SHA-256 of v1-basic's value_signed_bytes (the §4.1 chain)

vectors.name: create-head-inclusive
vectors.note: a push right after the create_environment entry (seq 3) itself, using it as the declared head (§6.3's inclusive convention): at head 3 env-prod-0001 is already created with epoch 1 valid, and the writer (member) is also valid since the seq-2 add

vectors.name: removed-writer-in-tenure
vectors.note: a past value within the membership interval (head 4 = its own rotate_epoch entry) by a writer removed at seq 5. It is the coordinates of a re-encryption push declaring the rotate entry itself as head (epoch 2 is valid at head 4 — inclusive), and it verifies under the key of that time even after the removal (§6.3-1)

vectors.name: env-dev-v1
vectors.note: version 1 (epoch 1) declaring env-dev-0002's own creation entry (seq 8) as the head

vectors.name: rotate-head-reencryption
vectors.note: a re-encryption push by the rotation executor (§7 = §4.1): the rotate_epoch entry (seq 10) itself is the declared head, the plaintext is identical but encrypted under the new epoch's DEK, and prev chains to the old epoch's version 1 (epoch monotonicity 2 ≥ 1)

vectors.name: listed-writer-in-scope
vectors.note: a push to an in-scope environment (env-dev-0002) by a listed writer (member listed{dev, stage} at head 19) passes (the permissive side of 3′)

vectors.name: second-device-writer-in-scope
vectors.note: a second-device positive: a push to an in-scope environment (env-dev-0002) by allmember-0013's (member, all) CI box C (cap (member, listed{dev, stage}) — seq 27) passes (declared head 28 is inside C's validity interval)

fork_same_version.note: two valid signatures with different contents on the same coordinates (var-api-key-0001 × version 3). Each branch alone passes all §6.3 checks (both verify successfully); as a pair, the difference in signed_bytes_sha256_hex becomes non-repudiable evidence of server equivocation (§14.2-5 — evidence, not prevention; detection is by comparing the same coordinates)

branches.name: fork-branch-a
branches.note: version 3 branch A (signed by the admin)

branches.name: fork-branch-b
branches.note: version 3 branch B (signed by the owner). Same coordinates and same prev as A but different contents

negative.name: tampered-signature
negative.note: flipping the last 1 bit of the signature bytes themselves fails verification

negative.name: tampered-ciphertext
negative.note: flipping the last 1 bit of the ciphertext (a substitution including the tag) fails verification of the original signature

negative.name: tampered-nonce
negative.note: tampering with the nonce fails verification of the original signature (the nonce is also signed)

negative.name: transplant-project
negative.note: a coordinate transplant to another project fails signature verification

negative.name: transplant-environment
negative.note: a coordinate transplant to another environment fails signature verification

negative.name: transplant-epoch
negative.note: a coordinate transplant to another epoch fails signature verification

negative.name: transplant-variable
negative.note: a coordinate transplant to another variable fails signature verification

negative.name: transplant-version
negative.note: a coordinate transplant to another version fails signature verification

negative.name: transplant-signer
negative.note: substituting writer_user_id fails verification even under the same key (protects against relabeling attribution — §4.1's user_id burning)

negative.name: wrong-signer-key
negative.note: verification fails under a non-signer key (blocks verification under a different key via FP relabeling)

negative.name: chain-head-swap
negative.note: substituting chain_head_hash_hex (keeping seq) fails signature verification (protects against relabeling the authorization time)

negative.name: chain-head-seq-mismatch
negative.note: substituting chain_head_seq (keeping the hash) fails signature verification (both hash and seq are signed)

negative.name: tampered-prev-hash
negative.note: substituting prev_value_sig_hash_hex fails verification of the original signature (chain tampering is pinned by the signature)

negative.name: suite-mismatch
negative.note: a different suite means a different domain string, so cross-suite signature transplants fail verification

negative.name: head-not-in-chain
negative.note: seq 12 exists in the local view but the hash does not match = hard evidence of a chain fork (equivocation) or forgery — reject immediately (§6.3-2a)

negative.name: head-beyond-local-seq
negative.note: seq 25 is beyond the local view's head (24) = the local chain may merely be stale. Resync first, accept if it matches as an extension, else it is evidence of a fork (§6.3-2b). This reason code pins the entry of the 'do not reject immediately — try resyncing' branch

negative.name: writer-role-insufficient
negative.note: at head 6, user-admin-0003 is a reader (the change_role is seq 7). A value push needs member-or-above at the declared-head time (§6.3-3)

negative.name: writer-removed-at-head
negative.note: reject the form where a writer removed at seq 5 declares a post-removal head (12) (blocks fresh writes by a removed member's key — §6.3-3)

negative.name: epoch-not-current-at-head
negative.note: at head 12, env-prod-0001's current epoch is 2. A signature on epoch 1 is rejected (the contrapositive of the path that forges a current-epoch value with a removed member's key — §6.3-4)

negative.name: head-before-environment-create
negative.note: the declared head (seq 2) is before env-prod-0001's create_environment (seq 3) = the environment does not exist and no epoch is defined. Implementations must not fall back to a default value (§6.3-4 latter part)

negative.name: key-from-other-tenure
negative.note: the combination old-key (from the first membership interval) × new-interval head (25) under the user_id that went remove → re-add-with-different-keys (derived chain seq 25) is rejected (§6.3-1's head-time key binding — an implementation that erased tenure by deduping on the same key fails here)

negative.name: writer-unknown-in-history
negative.note: a writer_user_id / key FP pair that exists at no point in the chain history cannot select a verification key and is rejected (the signature itself is valid under this negative's key)

negative.name: v1-nonempty-prev
negative.note: version 1's prev_value_sig_hash_hex must be the empty string (§4.1). A rule whose form must always be checked even in latest-only verification (session-14 ruling B)

negative.name: v2-empty-prev
negative.note: version > 1's prev_value_sig_hash_hex must be 64-char hex (§4.1). The form is always checked even by a latest-only verification that keeps no predecessor (ruling B)

negative.name: prev-hash-mismatch
negative.note: a chain inconsistency where prev does not match the known previous version (v1-basic)'s signed_bytes hash (§6.3-6). The signature is valid — it must not be crushed into an Ed25519 failure (ruling B)

negative.name: epoch-regression-across-versions
negative.note: version 3's epoch (1) is smaller than the previous version (v2-chained, epoch 2) = a §4.1 epoch-monotonicity violation. head 3 is inside the writer (member)'s membership interval and epoch 1 was the current epoch then — the form 'injecting an old epoch onto a forward version' that passes all other checks

negative.name: writer-environment-out-of-scope
negative.note: at head 19, user-devmember-0010 is member listed{dev, stage}. A signature on out-of-scope env-prod-0001 is rejected by the declared-head-time scope check (3′) even though role (member or above) is satisfied

negative.name: writer-role-precedes-scope
negative.note: at head 24, user-devmember-0010 is reader listed{dev} (applied at seq 22). An insufficient-role × out-of-scope compound violation is judged with the role check (3) preceding the scope check (3′)

negative.name: writer-scope-precedes-epoch
negative.note: an out-of-scope × old-epoch (1 — the current epoch at head 19 is 2) compound violation is judged with the scope check (3′) preceding epoch consistency (4)

negative.name: writer-device-revoked-at-head
negative.note: a signature by device C — revoked at seq 37 — declaring a post-revocation head (37) is writer-key-mismatch-at-head (a device's validity interval = after add_device until just before revoke_device. The person [allmember] stays enrolled — the same existing reason code as a membership-interval crossing)

negative.name: writer-device-role-insufficient
negative.note: the effective role of owner-0015's cap-(reader, all) device L (seq 29) is min(owner, reader) = reader. Even though the person is an owner, a value push by this device is writer-role-insufficient-at-head

negative.name: writer-device-environment-out-of-scope
negative.note: CI box C's effective scope is all ∩ {dev, stage} = {dev, stage}. Even though the person (allmember)'s scope is all, a signature on env-prod-0001 outside the device scope is writer-environment-out-of-scope-at-head

negative.name: writer-device-unknown-before-add
negative.note: a signature by C declaring head 26 — before C's add_device (seq 27) — is writer-key-mismatch-at-head (the start boundary of the validity interval — a device not yet added is not bound to the person)
